ideas.reasoning: R-103 remains the first useful comparison: it tests reward-trained state-conditioned corrections against independent draws and ARS, which an interface-check failure cannot settle. The implementer's distinction is technically relevant: action order follows the sorted actuator indices, not the configuration-list order, so prefer a narrowly documented assertion repair and one fresh-seed smoke over closing and duplicating the study. Its weakest point remains three training blocks, limiting conclusions about learner superiority even if the selected finalists differ.

question: R-103 stopped at its smoke gate before any training or evaluation, as the protocol requires. Six of seven gates passed on seed 4763 (128 envs, 720 steps, 514 episodes started): zero-theta identity 0 mismatches over 43,014 env-steps; filter reset 0 violations over 128 reset events; executed authority differs-fraction 1.00, pooled executed/proposed 0.991, 20/20 joints at ratio >= 0.25 (lowest THJ4 0.86, saturated 16% of steps; MFJ2 0.99, LFJ1 0.97 under the reference with its residual); likelihood ratio exactly 1, KL 0, all 32 gradients finite and nonzero; reconstruction 0 mismatches over 40 steps x 124 envs; throughput 3,652 transitions/s (projected 1.13 h). The seventh, the joint-order assertion, failed, and the cause is a defect in MY implementation of the check, not in the actor: the child compared the actor's joint table against env.cfg.actuated_joint_names, which is Isaac Lab's config list in finger order (WRJ1 WRJ0 FFJ3 FFJ2 FFJ1 MFJ3 ...). The env sorts actuated_dof_indices (inhand_manipulation_env.py lines 41-44), so action i drives hand.joint_names[sorted_idx[i]], i.e. the order the repo has used since R-039 (WRJ1 WRJ0 FFJ3 MFJ3 RFJ3 LFJ4 THJ4 FFJ2 ...; controllers.py, coordinate_repair.ACTION_ORDER, incumbent_residual.ACTUATED = 0..16,20,21,23). Under the agreed stopping rules I have not relaunched anything. Proposed amendment, for your agreement before any further simulator step: (1) fix that one comparison (and nothing else in the frozen configuration: same actor, reward, learners, schedule, thresholds, manifests, training seeds 4760-4762); (2) keep the failed attempt's artifacts under logs/pen_spin/r103_symbolic_reward/attempt1_smoke_joint_check/ and report it as a deviation; (3) rerun the whole smoke gate once on a NEW unspent seed 4770 instead of the consumed 4763 (so normalisation statistics and the probe signs come from 4770; 4763 stays spent and is recorded), adding 514 episodes started to the count against the unchanged 20,000 ceiling; (4) if the rerun passes all seven gates, continue the protocol unchanged; if any gate fails again, stop and close R-103 as inconclusive. Do you agree, or do you want a different handling (for example reusing 4763 because the smoke is reference-only, or closing R-103 and re-proposing)?
